purpose: Inputs of the batch-1 power levers of the Qwen3-8B ROM reticle (tools/qwen_power_levers.py -> results/arch/qwen_power_levers.json). Each lever is a NAMED scenario against the baseline of configs/hardware/power_scenarios.json; nothing here changes the baseline. Evidence classes as configs/hardware/power_scenarios.json evidence_classes. Conservative rule as there: where sources disagree take the value that makes the die hotter.

density_bytes_per_mm2.boundary: usable SRAM macro density at N6: 24.07 Mb/mm2 = HD bitcell 0.027 um2 (N7 = N6) at 0.65 array efficiency (bitcell over macro incl. decoders, sense amps, redundancy); the value tools/arch_budget_qwen3.SRAM_BITS_PER_MM2 sizes the KV prefetch buffer with (18.67 MB in 6.2 mm2)
density_bytes_per_mm2.source: configs/hardware/technology.json nodes.N6.sram_hd_bitcell_um2 (derived from https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/1989) and sram.array_efficiency (assumed, 0.55-0.75); tools/arch_budget_qwen3.py SRAM_BITS_PER_MM2

resident_read_j_per_byte.boundary: one byte read from a large on-die SRAM holding resident KV: the A100 L1's WHOLE measured access energy (control 1.26 + datapath 0.33 = 1.59 pJ/bit), i.e. the top of technology.json's sram_read_j_per_byte range, 4.9x the 2.6 pJ/B the baseline charges its KV ring. Charged IN ADDITION to the ring's write + read + delivery, which the resident bytes still pay (no credit for a direct SRAM-to-lane path).
resident_read_j_per_byte.source: Antepara, Zhao, Austin, Ding, Oliker, Wright, Williams, Benchmark-driven Models for Energy Analysis and Attribution of GPU-Accelerated Supercomputing, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 3 (as quoted in configs/hardware/technology.json energy.sram_read_j_per_byte.range_high)
resident_read_j_per_byte.quote: A100 L1: control 1.26 / datapath 0.33 / total 1.59 pJ/bit

tpuv4i_1mb_sram_7nm.boundary: one 64-bit access of a single-bank 1 MB SRAM at 7 nm (7.1 pJ / 8 B); a design estimate; the resident KV read is charged 14x this
tpuv4i_1mb_sram_7nm.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2, doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010
tpuv4i_1mb_sram_7nm.quote: 'Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm. Memory is pJ per 64-bit access.' ... '1 MB SRAM 100.000 14.000 7.1'

dally_hotchips2023_mb_sram.boundary: 'On-Chip SRAM MB' access, 50 pJ per 32-bit word (45 nm-era table): the order of the charged 12.72 pJ/B

tsmc_n5_bitcell.boundary: N5 6T HD bitcell (the N6 bitcell charged is 0.027, i.e. 29% larger: conservative); no macro-level Mb/mm2 found
tsmc_n5_bitcell.quote: 'A 135-Mb 0.021-um2 6-T high-density SRAM bit cell ... 5-nm HK-metal gate FinFET with EUV'

hbm_controller.note: Lever 2 (fixed-function streaming controller = a measured PHY + a sourced controller-logic estimate). Re-searched 2026-09-28: no measured host-side HBM2E/HBM3/HBM3E PHY energy per bit and no memory-controller logic energy per bit was found in any loadable source (SK hynix HBM3 JSSC 2023 doi:10.1109/JSSC.2022.3193354 and Samsung HBM3 JSSC 2023 doi:10.1109/JSSC.2022.3232096 abstracts state bandwidth and relative efficiency only; Rambus/Synopsys/Cadence PHY pages give no pJ/bit). The only interface figures are MODELS (O'Connor MICRO 2017: interposer I/O 0.80 pJ/b at 50% activity; Chatterjee HPCA 2017: 0.54 pJ/b) and measured die-to-die links that are not HBM PHYs (LIPINCON 0.56 pJ/bit, GRS 0.54 pJ/b). The lever therefore CANNOT be built from measured parts: scenario_die_pj_per_bit is null and the record carries only the requirement (the die share that would reach the target) and the existing sensitivities (GH200 8.23, the withdrawn 0.8 I/O floor) for scale.

oconnor_micro2017_io.boundary: HBM2 interposer I/O, both ends, 50% toggle; MODEL (28 nm DRAM parameters after Rambus), no controller
oconnor_micro2017_io.source: O'Connor et al., Fine-Grained DRAM, MICRO 2017, Table 3, https://www.cs.utexas.edu/users/skeckler/pubs/MICRO_2017_Fine_Grained_DRAM.pdf

chatterjee_hpca2017_io.boundary: HBM data transfer on the interposer only, 50% toggle; MODEL; no controller
chatterjee_hpca2017_io.source: Chatterjee et al., Architecting an Energy-Efficient DRAM System for GPUs, HPCA 2017, https://d1qx31qr3h6wln.cloudfront.net/publications/HPCA_2017_Subchannels.pdf
chatterjee_hpca2017_io.quote: the rest of the datapath consumes 2.85pJ/b at 50% toggle rate (2.31 pJ/b for column, 0.54 pJ/b for I/O)

lipincon_cowos_link.boundary: TSMC 7 nm CoWoS die-to-die parallel link (8 Gb/s/pin, 0.3 V swing, unterminated), TX+RX; a die-to-die link, NOT an HBM PHY, no controller
lipincon_cowos_link.source: Lin et al., A 7-nm 4-GHz Arm-Core-Based CoWoS Chiplet Design for High-Performance Computing, IEEE JSSC 2020, doi:10.1109/JSSC.2019.2960207 (abstract)
lipincon_cowos_link.quote: The scalable link module offers 320 GB/s of aggregate bandwidth, operating at 8.0 Gb/s/pin and 0.3-V transmitter swing without receiver termination to achieve 0.56-pJ/bit energy efficiency and 1.6-Tb/s/mm2 bandwidth density.

hmc_gen1_whole_cube.boundary: Micron HMC Gen1 whole cube (DRAM + logic base die with vault controllers + SerDes), from IDD7; no logic-die split
hmc_gen1_whole_cube.source: Pawlowski, Hybrid Memory Cube (HMC), Hot Chips 23, 2011, slide 21

link_j_per_bit.boundary: UCIe advanced-package link, both ends; the top of the UCIe target range (the measured 3 nm best case is 0.29, TSMC's 7 nm CoWoS LIPINCON 0.56)
link_j_per_bit.source: configs/hardware/technology.json energy.link_j_per_bit.ucie_advanced.range_high (UCIe Consortium, Hot Chips 2023 tutorial, Electrical Summary)

d2d_bytes_s.boundary: die-to-die bandwidth each direction, sized to carry half of a die's KV (the remote 3 stacks) at the 6-stack sustained 5.4 TB/s during its stage: 2.7 TB/s = 21.6 Tb/s each way. Blackwell's shipping die-to-die link is 10 TB/s (NVIDIA), so the rate is shipped practice; the area is priced from a measured link below.
d2d_bytes_s.source: tools/arch_budget_qwen3.py requirements.kv_hbm.sustained_bytes_s / 2; NVIDIA Blackwell architecture page ('10 TB/s chip-to-chip interconnect')

d2d_phy_mm2.boundary: die-to-die PHY area on EACH die for 2 x 21.6 Tb/s (both directions) at LIPINCON's measured 1.6 Tb/s/mm2 area density (7 nm, 8 Gb/s/pin): 43.2 / 1.6 = 27 mm2; the 3 nm UCIe test chip's 5.27 Tb/s/mm shoreline would need ~8.2 mm of the edge the 3 dropped stacks free
d2d_phy_mm2.source: Lin et al., IEEE JSSC 2020, doi:10.1109/JSSC.2019.2960207 (abstract); configs/hardware/technology.json energy.link_j_per_bit.ucie_advanced (JSSC 2026 doi:10.1109/JSSC.2026.3651425)
d2d_phy_mm2.quote: '0.56-pJ/bit energy efficiency and 1.6-Tb/s/mm2 bandwidth density'; 'exhibit 0.29 pJ/bit power efficiency with 5.27Tb/s/mm ... and 3.5 ns measured FDI-to-FDI latency'

hop_latency_s.boundary: one die-to-die crossing, FDI to FDI (adapter + PHY both ends), 3 nm CoWoS UCIe test chip; charged once per hop plus the hop's bytes at d2d_bytes_s

hop_bytes_per_slot.boundary: one slot's BF16 hidden state (4,096 x 2 B) per hop; with DFlash each hop carries the drafter's 5 tapped layers' states (x5), 4 hops a step (verify A->B, token back, draft taps both ways)
hop_bytes_per_slot.source: Qwen3-8B config.json hidden_size 4096 (tools/hdc_timing.SHAPES); z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16 fc input 5 x 4096 (tools/dflash_step_timing.DFLASH_FC)

package_ratings.note: the two-die per-die and per-package limits are the baseline's own (configs/hardware/power_scenarios.json cooling.references b200_hgx 1,000 W air and gb200_nvl72 1,200 W liquid, each less its 8 stacks at peak, per die): 374.6 W air / 474.6 W liquid a die, 1,000 / 1,200 W a package

dvfs.note: Lever 4. The only sourced V/f relation for the node is a vendor OPP (operating performance point) table of a TSMC N6 SoC's GPU. It is transferred by NORMALISING to its top point: our routed 1.0986 GHz is taken to sit at the table's top (0.75 V) and a lower clock at the table's relative voltage. What scales: core dynamic energy per operation and clock power (x V^2, clock also x f); what does not: leakage (no credit, conservative), stack idle, and the HBM die share (the PHY/controller energy per bit is charged at the measured path, whose I/O supply is not the core rail). The batch-1 step is compute-chain bound (123,301 cycles against a 122,881-cycle KV stream at 8K), so the rate scales with f: DVFS lowers the per-user rate and can only raise the CAPPED rate.

curve.boundary: MediaTek MT8195 (Kompanio 1380, TSMC 6 nm) Mali-G57 GPU operating points as shipped in the mainline Linux device tree: vendor DVFS table (frequency, core supply), not a silicon measurement of our die; transferred by normalising to its top point
curve.quote: 'opp-hz = /bits/ 64 <880000000>; opp-microvolt = <750000>;' ... 'opp-hz = /bits/ 64 <390000000>; opp-microvolt = <625000>;'; MediaTek: 'Manufactured using the latest TSMC 6nm process', 'MediaTek Kompanio 1380 (MT8195T)'
curve.cross_check: Keller et al. (NVIDIA, TSMC 5 nm, measured) as summarised by Dally, Hot Chips 2023: 'Voltage range: 0.46V - 1.05V', 'Frequency range: 152 MHz - 1760 MHz' (range ends only; intermediate points unpublished)

not_evaluated.stacked_sram_die: a hybrid-bonded SRAM die over the logic (3D V-Cache class) could hold a whole 8K user KV (604 MB) off the reticle area, but no source gives the thermal derating of a cache die stacked on a ~550 W logic die, and the only shipping part (AMD 3D V-Cache, ISSCC 2022 doi:10.1109/ISSCC42614.2022.9731565: 'expands Zen3's on-die L3 Cache from 32MB to 96MB') is a ~100 W-class CPU; its die area was not verifiable. Not priced.
not_evaluated.hbm_controller_measured: no measured host PHY or controller energy per bit exists in a loadable source (see hbm_controller.note); the record gives the requirement instead (hbm_die_share_needed_for_target)
not_evaluated.kv_int4: 4-bit KV is a SENSITIVITY only (user rule); it is in the record as sensitivity_kv_int4 and not a lever
